name: ambient
title: Ambient
description: The soft olive or amber corner glow from the Lantern hero, as a decorative background layer.
notes: Ambient is absolutely positioned and hidden from screen readers. Put it inside a relative parent (add overflow-hidden to clip it) and keep the content after it positioned so it stays on top. Resize it with className, for example size-96.

name: code-block
title: Code Block
description: A code panel with a filename bar, language badge, copy button, optional line numbers and highlighted lines. No syntax highlighter required.
notes: Pass code as a plain string and it renders in the default terminal text color. To use your own highlighter, render its output as children instead, for example a div with shiki HTML, and set copyValue to the raw source.
Line numbers and highlighted lines apply to the code prop. Set maxHeight to cap the panel and scroll the rest.

name: command-tabs
title: Command Tabs
description: A package manager switcher that shows the same command for npm, pnpm, yarn and bun, with a copy button. The chosen manager is remembered and shared by every instance on the page.
notes: type="dlx" prefixes npx, pnpm dlx, yarn dlx or bunx --bun. type="install" prefixes npm install, pnpm add, yarn add or bun add.
Pass commands, a record keyed by npm, pnpm, yarn and bun, to write each command out yourself. The last choice is saved in localStorage under lantern-package-manager.

name: console
title: Console
description: TurtleDeck's log console: timestamped lines in four levels that stay scrolled to the newest entry, over a command row with an orange prompt.
usage:
<Console className="h-80">
  <ConsoleLines>
    <ConsoleLine level="system" time="14:02:10">Connected to quarry-2</ConsoleLine>
    <ConsoleLine level="error" time="14:02:19">Lava found</ConsoleLine>
  </ConsoleLines>
  <ConsoleInput onCommand={(cmd) => run(cmd)} />
</Console>
notes: Levels are info (foreground), system (muted), error (destructive) and input (green, with a prompt glyph). ConsoleLines only follows new lines while the reader is at the bottom, so scrolling up to read history is not interrupted.
ConsoleInput clears itself on submit and keeps a history you can step through with the up and down arrow keys. Try help, fuel, pos, inv, dig, home and clear in the demo.

name: control-pad
title: Control Pad
description: The TurtleDeck movement pad: a 3x3 grid of buttons with icons, labels and key hints. Optional keyboard binding presses the matching button.
notes: Set keyboard="pad" to listen only while focus is inside the pad, or keyboard="page" to listen anywhere. Keys typed into inputs, textareas and editable content are ignored, as are shortcuts with Ctrl, Cmd or Alt.
Pass actions to change the layout. Each action has an id, label, icon and key; use null for an empty cell. Held keys fire onAction once and show the button pressed until released.

name: directory-card
title: Directory Card
description: The Lantern directory listing: a grid banner with an icon and hub address, category, title, description, tags and a status footer.
usage: Community Lantern Guestbook Leave a note. Online
notes: With asChild the whole card becomes the link, and it lifts with a block shadow on hover. The footer status takes online, busy, offline or error.

name: eyebrow
title: Eyebrow
description: The mono uppercase label that sits above Lantern headings.

name: guestbook
title: Guestbook
description: A list of signed messages with a composer, like the Lantern guestbook. Entries show initials, a name, relative time and the message.
notes: GuestbookEntry takes time as a Date, timestamp or ISO string and shows it as relative time that refreshes every minute. Any other string is shown as written.
GuestbookComposer keeps its own draft, counts characters against maxLength (280 by default) and calls onSign with the trimmed message. Ctrl or Cmd plus Enter also signs.

name: inventory-grid
title: Inventory Grid
description: TurtleDeck's inventory: square slots on a faint grid with beveled item swatches, short names and stack counts. The selected slot gets an orange border and the arrow keys move it.
usage:
<InventoryGrid aria-label="Turtle inventory" defaultValue={0}>
  <InventorySlot name="Cobble" count={64} color="#8b8f88" />
  <InventorySlot />
</InventoryGrid>
notes: The grid uses role=grid with one tab stop. Arrow keys move the selection, Home and End jump to the ends of a row, and Ctrl+Home or Ctrl+End jump to the first or last slot.
Set columns to change the width, for example columns={9} for a chest, and size="sm" to hide item names for tight layouts. Use value and onValueChange to control the selection.

name: key-reveal
title: Key Reveal
description: TurtleDeck's show-once key box: the key in mono type with a copy button, an optional masked mode with a reveal toggle, and a warning that it will not be shown again.
notes: Pass warning={null} to hide the warning line, or your own text to replace it. onCopy fires after the key reaches the clipboard.

name: navbar
title: Navbar
description: The Lantern site header: diamond mark, name and outlined tag, nav links and a bordered call to action. On phones the links move into a sheet behind a menu button.
usage:
<Navbar>
  <NavbarBrand href="/">
    <NavbarMark />
    lantern
    <NavbarLabel>Hub</NavbarLabel>
  </NavbarBrand>
  <NavbarLinks>
    <NavbarLink href="/directory" active>Directory</NavbarLink>
    <NavbarCta href="/publish">Publish a hub</NavbarCta>
  </NavbarLinks>
  <NavbarMobile>
    <NavbarLink href="/directory" active>Directory</NavbarLink>
    <NavbarCta href="/publish">Publish a hub</NavbarCta>
  </NavbarMobile>
</Navbar>
notes: NavbarBrand, NavbarLink and NavbarCta accept asChild, so you can pass a framework Link.
NavbarMobile shows below the md breakpoint. Pass it the same links as NavbarLinks. Following a link closes the sheet.

name: orbit
title: Orbit
description: The dashed elliptical rings behind the Lantern hero terminal, as a decorative background layer with optional slow rotation.
notes: Orbit is absolutely positioned and hidden from screen readers. Place it inside a relative parent, before the content it sits behind; that content should be positioned (Terminal already is) so it paints on top.
spin rotates the rings slowly in alternating directions and is skipped when the visitor prefers reduced motion. Pass OrbitRing children to lay out rings yourself.

name: server-card
title: Server Card
description: A Minecraft server status card with a copyable address, online state, a player bar, version badge, MOTD and an initials stack of who is on.
usage:
<ServerCard
  name="Lantern SMP"
  address="play.example.net"
  players={7}
  maxPlayers={20}
  version="1.21.4"
/>

name: stat
title: Stat
description: The numbers strip from the Lantern site: large orange figures with a muted caption, split by dividers and stacked on mobile.
notes: StatGroup renders a description list. Put StatLabel before StatValue in the markup so screen readers read the term first; the value is shown on top visually.

name: status-dot
title: Status Dot
description: A small glowing dot for online, running, error and offline states. Pulses by default.

name: status-pill
title: Status Pill
description: The TurtleDeck status label: a colored dot and a mono uppercase word for online, offline, running and idle. Running pulses.
notes: With no children the pill shows the tone name. Add ml-auto through className to push it to the end of a flex row.

name: terminal
title: Terminal
description: The in-game terminal window from the Lantern hero: title bar, address line, prompt lines, output and a blinking cursor.

name: typewriter
title: Typewriter
description: Terminal lines that type themselves out, with a pause between lines, an optional loop and a blinking cursor. Use it inside a Terminal or on its own.
usage:
<Terminal>
  <TerminalHeader>LANTERN</TerminalHeader>
  <TerminalTypewriter
    loop
    lines={[
      { prompt: true, text: "lantern publish ./site" },
      { text: "published hub://your-little-world/", delay: 800 },
    ]}
  />
</Terminal>
notes: Each line takes prompt, text, delay (milliseconds before it starts) and instant. Command lines (prompt: true) are typed at speed milliseconds per character; output lines print whole unless instant is false.
Visitors who prefer reduced motion see every line at once. Screen readers get the full text immediately from a visually hidden copy; the animated text is hidden from them.
The terminal grows as lines appear. Give the body a min height (bodyClassName on TerminalTypewriter, className on Typewriter) to keep the layout still.

name: button
title: Button
description: Orange primary actions and quiet outlined secondaries, with sizes, icons and link rendering.

examples.name: button-states
examples.title: Loading, disabled and as a link

name: button-group
title: Button Group
description: Joins buttons, inputs and text into one control with shared borders, laid out horizontally or vertically.
notes: Use orientation="vertical" to stack. Nest ButtonGroups to put gaps between sets.
Filled buttons have no border, so put a ButtonGroupSeparator between them, as in the split button. Give the group an aria-label when its purpose is not clear from the buttons.

name: calendar
title: Calendar
description: A month grid for picking a day or a range of days, built on React DayPicker with orange selection and today marked.
usage:
const [date, setDate] = React.useState<Date | undefined>(new Date());

<Calendar mode="single" selected={date} onSelect={setDate} />
notes: Every React DayPicker prop is passed through: mode, disabled, numberOfMonths, startMonth, endMonth, locale and so on.
Use captionLayout="dropdown" with startMonth and endMonth for jumping across years. Arrow keys move between days, Page Up and Page Down change month.

name: checkbox
title: Checkbox
description: A square toggle for yes or no choices, with checked, indeterminate and disabled states.
notes: Pass checked="indeterminate" to show a dash, for example on a select-all box when only some rows are checked.

name: combobox
title: Combobox
description: A searchable picker built from a popover and a command list, with a single-value Combobox and a multi-select ComboboxMulti that shows picks as badges.
usage:
<Combobox
  options={[{ value: "quarry", label: "quarry.hub" }]}
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  placeholder="Pick a server"
  searchPlaceholder="Search servers..."
  empty="No server found."
/>
notes: Options take a value, a label and optional keywords, icon and disabled. Search matches the value, label and keywords.
ComboboxMulti keeps the popover open while you pick. Backspace in an empty search removes the last pick.

name: copy-button
title: Copy Button
description: An icon button that copies a value to the clipboard and flashes a green check. Failures show a red cross instead of throwing.
usage: <CopyButton value="pastebin get Xk2p9 hub" label="Copy command" />
notes: Uses the Clipboard API and falls back to a hidden textarea on insecure origins. The result is announced through a polite live region.

name: date-picker
title: Date Picker
description: A button that opens a calendar in a popover, for picking a single date or a range, with optional presets.
usage:
const [date, setDate] = React.useState<Date | undefined>();

<DatePicker value={date} onChange={setDate} placeholder="Pick a date" />
notes: DateRangePicker shows two months side by side on wide screens and one month below 768px.

Presets take a label and a value or a function returning one, so relative dates like "Tomorrow" are worked out when clicked. Pass calendarProps to forward options such as disabled days to the calendar.

name: field
title: Field
description: Building blocks for accessible forms: labels, descriptions, errors, fieldsets and legends in vertical, horizontal or responsive layouts.
usage:
<FieldGroup>
  <Field>
    <FieldLabel htmlFor="name">Site name</FieldLabel>
    <Input id="name" />
    <FieldDescription>Shown in the directory.</FieldDescription>
  </Field>
  <Field orientation="horizontal">
    <Switch id="online" />
    <FieldLabel htmlFor="online">Keep site online</FieldLabel>
  </Field>
</FieldGroup>
notes: Set data-invalid on a Field and aria-invalid on its control to show an error. FieldError takes children or an errors array, such as the output of a schema validator.
Wrap a horizontal Field in a FieldLabel to turn a radio or checkbox into a selectable card.
orientation="responsive" stacks on narrow containers and goes side by side once the parent FieldGroup is wide enough.

name: form
title: Form
description: Form building blocks wired to react-hook-form, with zod validation, accessible labels, descriptions and error messages.
usage:
const form = useForm<z.infer<typeof schema>>({ resolver: zodResolver(schema) })

<Form {...form}>
  <form onSubmit={form.handleSubmit(onSubmit)}>
    <FormField
      control={form.control}
      name="name"
      render={({ field }) => (
        <FormItem>
          <FormLabel>Site name</FormLabel>
          <FormControl>
            <Input {...field} />
          </FormControl>
          <FormDescription>Shown in the hub directory.</FormDescription>
          <FormMessage />
        </FormItem>
      )}
    />
  </form>
</Form>
notes: FormControl passes the id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid to its child, so FormLabel, FormDescription and FormMessage are linked to the control automatically.
Field is the lighter option: the same layout without react-hook-form, for forms you validate yourself.

name: input
title: Input
description: A single-line text field for text, email, passwords and files, with invalid and disabled states.

name: input-group
title: Input Group
description: An input or textarea with icons, text prefixes like hub://, and inline buttons attached inside one border.
notes: Addons take align="inline-start", "inline-end", "block-start" or "block-end". Clicking an addon focuses the input.

name: input-otp
title: Input OTP
description: A row of single-character slots for pairing codes and one-time passwords, with paste support.
usage:
<InputOTP maxLength={6}>
  <InputOTPGroup>
    <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
  </InputOTPGroup>
  <InputOTPSeparator />
  <InputOTPGroup>
    <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={4} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={5} />
  </InputOTPGroup>
</InputOTP>
notes: Built on the input-otp package by Guilherme Rodz. Use the pattern prop to limit which characters are accepted.

name: label
title: Label
description: An accessible label for form controls.

name: native-select
title: Native Select
description: A styled native select element with the Input look, a chevron, options and option groups.
notes: Use Native Select when you want the platform picker, especially on phones, or need the value to work in a plain form post. Use Select for a fully styled dropdown with icons.
The wrapper is w-fit by default. Pass className="w-full" to stretch the select; the open list is drawn by the browser.

name: radio-group
title: Radio Group
description: A set of options where exactly one can be picked, navigable with the arrow keys.
notes: For choice cards, wrap each item in a Label and style the checked card with has-data-[state=checked]. The Field component does this for you with FieldLabel.

name: select
title: Select
description: A dropdown for picking one value from a list, with groups, labels, icons and full keyboard support.
usage:
<Select>
  <SelectTrigger className="w-48">
    <SelectValue placeholder="Pick a theme" />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="lantern">Lantern</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="moss">Moss</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>

name: slider
title: Slider
description: Pick a number or a range by dragging square thumbs along a track, or with the arrow keys.
notes: Pass two values to get a range with two thumbs. Give the slider an aria-label or aria-labelledby.

name: switch
title: Switch
description: An on and off control for settings that take effect right away.

name: tag-input
title: Tag Input
description: A text field that turns what you type into removable tags. Enter or comma adds a tag, Backspace on an empty field removes the last one, and pasting a comma separated list adds several.
usage:
<Label htmlFor="tags">Tags</Label>
<TagInput id="tags" defaultValue={["turtles"]} placeholder="Add a tag" />
notes: Use value and onValueChange to control it, or defaultValue to let it manage its own tags. Duplicates are ignored (case-insensitive unless caseSensitive is set).
max caps the count and validate(tag, tags) can reject a tag; onReject(tag, reason) reports why, with reason duplicate, invalid or max. Rejected text stays in the field so it can be fixed.
id, placeholder and aria-* props go to the text input, so a Label or FieldLabel points at it. Each remove button is labelled with its tag, and additions and removals are announced to screen readers.

name: textarea
title: Textarea
description: A multi-line text field that grows with its content, with invalid and disabled states.

name: toggle
title: Toggle
description: A button that stays pressed, for switching a single tool or view on and off.

name: toggle-group
title: Toggle Group
description: A row of toggles joined together, allowing one or many to be pressed.
usage:
<ToggleGroup type="single" variant="outline" defaultValue="left">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="left" aria-label="Align left">
    <AlignLeftIcon />
  </ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="right" aria-label="Align right">
    <AlignRightIcon />
  </ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>

name: accordion
title: Accordion
description: Stacked questions that open one panel at a time, with a rotating chevron and orange open state.
usage:
<Accordion type="single" collapsible>
  <AccordionItem value="a">
    <AccordionTrigger>What is Lantern?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>A small web for Minecraft servers.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

name: aspect-ratio
title: Aspect Ratio
description: Keeps media and placeholders at a fixed width to height ratio as the container resizes.
notes: The child fills the box absolutely, so give images size-full and object-cover. Put rounded corners and overflow-hidden on AspectRatio itself.

name: avatar
title: Avatar
description: A round player portrait with an image and mono initials as the fallback. Group several into an overlapping stack.

name: badge
title: Badge
description: Small mono labels, including the square outlined tag used for HUB and DEV.

name: card
title: Card
description: A panel with header, content and footer slots, plus the grid-patterned art banner from the Lantern directory.

name: carousel
title: Carousel
description: A swipeable row of slides with previous and next buttons and dot indicators. Built on Embla.
notes: Set a basis class on CarouselItem, such as basis-1/3, to show several slides at once.
The previous and next buttons sit outside the slides, 3rem to each side. Leave room for them with padding on the parent, or move them with className.
Arrow keys move between slides when focus is inside the carousel. Use setApi to reach the Embla API.

name: item
title: Item
description: A flexible row for lists of things: media, title, description and actions, with outline and muted variants.
notes: Use asChild to render an Item as a link; it picks up a hover state automatically.
ItemGroup has role="list". Wrap each Item in an element with role="listitem", or pass role="listitem" to the Item.

name: kbd
title: Kbd
description: Mono key caps for keyboard shortcuts. KbdGroup lines several keys up with even spacing.

name: separator
title: Separator
description: A one-pixel rule in the border color, horizontal or vertical.

name: table
title: Table
description: A plain, responsive table with mono uppercase column heads, hover rows, a footer and a caption. Scrolls sideways on narrow screens.

examples.name: table-compact
examples.title: Compact data with a footer total

name: timeline
title: Timeline
description: A vertical changelog or roadmap: a dot or icon on a connecting line, a mono date or version label, a title and a description, marked done, current or planned.
usage:
<Timeline>
  <TimelineItem state="done">
    <TimelineLabel>v0.2 / 2026-05</TimelineLabel>
    <TimelineTitle>Guestbooks</TimelineTitle>
    <TimelineDescription>Visitors can sign a page.</TimelineDescription>
  </TimelineItem>
  <TimelineItem state="current">...</TimelineItem>
</Timeline>
notes: States: done (green), current (orange, marked aria-current="step") and planned (muted, dashed). Each item announces its state to screen readers. Pass icon to swap the dot for a boxed lucide icon, and size="compact" for dense changelogs.
Put Badge components inside TimelineTitle to tag an entry.

name: typography
title: Typography
description: Long-form text styles: headings, paragraphs, lead, lists, quotes, inline code and tables as small components, plus a Prose wrapper that styles raw HTML or rendered markdown.
usage:
<TypographyH1>Publishing a hub site</TypographyH1>
<TypographyP>Run <TypographyInlineCode>lantern seed</TypographyInlineCode> once.</TypographyP>

<Prose dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />
notes: Prose styles descendant h1 to h4, p, a, strong, ul, ol, blockquote, code, pre, hr, table and img with plain Tailwind classes, so it does not need @tailwindcss/typography. Wrap part of the content in an element with the not-prose class to leave everything inside it unstyled.
Links are orange, list markers are green mono, blockquotes get an orange left rule and code uses the terminal colors.

name: chart
title: Chart
description: Recharts v3 wrappers: a responsive ChartContainer driven by a ChartConfig of series labels and colors, plus a Lantern tooltip and legend. Axes and grid lines pick up border and muted colors.
notes: Every key in the config becomes a --color-<key> variable on the container, so series can use fill="var(--color-fuel)". Keys without a color fall back to var(--chart-1) through var(--chart-5) in order.
ChartContainer uses aspect-video by default. Pass aspect-auto with a fixed height, or aspect-square with a max height for pie and radial charts.

name: data-table
title: Data Table
description: A reusable TanStack Table v9 data table with a global filter, sortable headers, a column visibility menu, row selection and pagination, built on the Lantern table, input, checkbox, dropdown menu and select.
notes: Columns are TanStack Table v9 column defs typed with the exported dataTableFeatures. Use createDataTableColumnHelper<TData>() so accessor values keep their types.

Set meta.title for the label in the column menu and meta.className for per-column classes such as text-right. Turn parts off with filterable={false}, columnToggle={false} or pagination={false}, and pass toolbar={(table) => ...} to add controls beside the filter.

name: collapsible
title: Collapsible
description: Shows and hides a section of content with an animated height.

name: direction
title: Direction
description: Sets the reading direction for Radix components below it, so menus, selects and sliders mirror correctly in right to left layouts.
notes: The provider only tells Radix components the direction. Also set the dir attribute on the html element or a wrapper so text, flex order and logical utilities like ps-* and start-* flip.
useDirection returns the current direction, handy for flipping icons such as arrows.

name: drawer
title: Drawer
description: A bottom sheet with a grab handle that can be dragged closed. Built on vaul.

examples.name: drawer-responsive
examples.title: Dialog on desktop, drawer on mobile

usage:
<Drawer>
  <DrawerTrigger asChild>
    <Button>Open</Button>
  </DrawerTrigger>
  <DrawerContent>
    <DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerTitle>Refuel miner-02</DrawerTitle>
      <DrawerDescription>Pick how much coal to load.</DrawerDescription>
    </DrawerHeader>
    <DrawerFooter>
      <DrawerClose asChild>
        <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
      </DrawerClose>
    </DrawerFooter>
  </DrawerContent>
</Drawer>
notes: Pass direction="top", "left" or "right" to Drawer to slide from another edge. The grab handle only shows on bottom drawers.

name: resizable
title: Resizable
description: Panels split by draggable handles, for editors and dashboards. Built on react-resizable-panels.
notes: This uses react-resizable-panels v4. The group takes orientation (not direction). Sizes given as numbers are pixels; use strings like "40%" for percentages.
Handles are keyboard accessible: focus one with Tab and use the arrow keys. Double-click a handle to reset its panel.

name: scroll-area
title: Scroll Area
description: A scroll container with a thin custom scrollbar that turns orange on hover.
notes: For sideways scrolling add <ScrollBar orientation="horizontal" /> inside the ScrollArea and give the content w-max.

name: sidebar
title: Sidebar
description: A composable app sidebar that collapses off canvas or down to icons, and turns into a sheet on phones.
notes: SidebarProvider holds the open state in React state only; nothing is written to cookies. Pass open and onOpenChange to control it yourself. Cmd+B or Ctrl+B toggles it; set keyboardShortcut={false} when a page has more than one sidebar.
Set variant to sidebar, floating or inset, and collapsible to offcanvas, icon or none. Below 768px the sidebar opens as a sheet from SidebarTrigger.
The sidebar is fixed to the viewport by default. To embed it in a box, give SidebarProvider className="relative h-full min-h-0" and Sidebar className="absolute h-full", as the examples here do.
The use-mobile hook is installed alongside the component at hooks/use-mobile.ts.

name: alert-dialog
title: Alert Dialog
description: A modal that interrupts to confirm an important action. It does not close on outside click, so the reader has to choose.
usage:
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="destructive">Unpublish site</Button>
  </AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogHeader>
      <AlertDialogTitle>Unpublish site?</AlertDialogTitle>
      <AlertDialogDescription>Visitors will see a dead link.</AlertDialogDescription>
    </AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogFooter>
      <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
      <AlertDialogAction variant="destructive">Unpublish</AlertDialogAction>
    </AlertDialogFooter>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>
notes: AlertDialogAction takes variant="destructive" for a filled red confirm button.

name: context-menu
title: Context Menu
description: A menu opened by right-clicking an area, with labels, shortcuts, checkbox and radio items and submenus.
notes: On touch devices the menu opens on a long-press instead of a right-click. From the keyboard, focus the trigger and press Shift F10 or the context menu key.
The API matches Dropdown Menu: ContextMenuItem takes inset and variant="destructive", and there are checkbox, radio and sub items.

name: dialog
title: Dialog
description: A modal window over a dimmed backdrop, for short forms and focused reading. Focus is trapped inside and Escape closes it.
usage: Edit profile. Change how you appear on the network.
notes: The orange period after the title is a Lantern touch you add in the title content. It is not forced by the component.
Pass showCloseButton={false} to DialogContent to hide the corner close button.

name: dropdown-menu
title: Dropdown Menu
description: A menu of actions opened from a button, with labels, separators, shortcuts, checkbox and radio items and submenus.

name: hover-card
title: Hover Card
description: A preview card that opens when a pointer rests on a link, such as a creator profile behind a username.
notes: Hover cards are for sighted pointer users. The trigger link should still lead somewhere useful on its own.

name: popover
title: Popover
description: A small floating panel anchored to a trigger, for quick settings and short forms.

name: sheet
title: Sheet
description: A dialog that slides in from an edge of the screen, for settings panels and mobile navigation.
usage:
<Sheet>
  <SheetTrigger asChild>
    <Button>Open</Button>
  </SheetTrigger>
  <SheetContent side="right">
    <SheetHeader>
      <SheetTitle>Server settings</SheetTitle>
      <SheetDescription>Where your hub is hosted.</SheetDescription>
    </SheetHeader>
  </SheetContent>
</Sheet>
notes: Set side to top, right, bottom or left. Left and right sheets take three quarters of the screen on phones and cap at 24rem on larger screens.

name: tooltip
title: Tooltip
description: A dark label in small mono type that appears on hover or keyboard focus. Good for naming icon buttons.
notes: Each Tooltip brings its own provider. Wrap a group in TooltipProvider to share the open delay so moving between buttons shows the next tooltip instantly.
Tooltips do not show on touch screens. Keep an aria-label on icon-only buttons.

name: breadcrumb
title: Breadcrumb
description: Shows where a page sits in the site, in small mono uppercase with chevron separators.
notes: The collapsed example uses the Dropdown Menu component, which you install separately.

name: command
title: Command
description: A searchable command palette with grouped items and shortcuts, inline or in a dialog opened with Cmd K.
notes: Arrow keys move the selection and Enter runs the item. CommandDialog wraps the palette in the Lantern dialog; wire up your own Cmd K / Ctrl K listener to toggle it.

name: file-tree
title: File Tree
description: An accessible tree of folders and files with indentation guides, an orange selected border and status letters like M for modified.
usage:
<FileTree
  items={[{ id: "pages", name: "pages", children: [{ id: "index", name: "index.lua" }] }]}
  onSelect={(item) => open(item)}
/>
notes: Follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern: Up and Down move, Right expands or enters a folder, Left collapses or moves to the parent, Home and End jump, Enter or Space selects, * expands siblings and typing a letter jumps to the next matching name.
An item with a children array is a folder. Selection and expansion can be controlled or uncontrolled.

name: menubar
title: Menubar
description: A row of menus like a desktop app's menu bar, with shortcuts, checkbox and radio items and submenus.
notes: Once a menu is open, Left and Right arrows move between menus and hovering another trigger switches to it. Item parts share the Dropdown Menu API.

name: navigation-menu
title: Navigation Menu
description: A header menu whose triggers open panels of links in a shared viewport, with an orange indicator under the open trigger.
notes: Below 768px the panel fills the width of the menu and links stack in one column; give panel contents md: widths for the wide layout.
Pass viewport={false} to render each panel under its own trigger instead of in the shared viewport. Put NavigationMenuIndicator last inside the list.

name: pagination
title: Pagination
description: Page links with previous and next controls. The current page gets an orange outline.
notes: The Prev and Next words hide on phones to leave room for the page numbers.

name: stepper
title: Stepper
description: Numbered steps with zero-padded mono numbers in bordered squares. Complete steps turn green with a check and the current step is orange.
usage:
<Stepper>
  <StepperItem state="complete">
    <StepperTitle>Place a computer</StepperTitle>
    <StepperDescription>Attach a modem.</StepperDescription>
  </StepperItem>
  <StepperItem state="current">
    <StepperTitle>Run the installer</StepperTitle>
  </StepperItem>
</Stepper>
notes: Numbers come from a CSS counter, so steps number themselves. The horizontal orientation uses a container query and stacks vertically when its container is narrower than 36rem. The current step gets aria-current="step".

name: tabs
title: Tabs
description: Mono uppercase tabs with an orange underline on the active tab, plus a boxed variant for switching between panels.
notes: Set variant="boxed" on Tabs to get the segmented style. The list and triggers pick it up automatically.
The tab list scrolls sideways when there are more tabs than fit on a phone.

name: alert
title: Alert
description: An inline callout with an icon, title and description. Default, success, warning and destructive variants each carry a colored left edge.
usage:
<Alert variant="warning">
  <TriangleAlert />
  <AlertTitle>Low fuel</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>Drop coal in the turtle.</AlertDescription>
</Alert>

name: announcement-bar
title: Announcement Bar
description: A slim full-width bar for the top of a site with an optional badge, a message, a link and a dismiss button that can remember the dismissal.
usage:
<AnnouncementBar id="directory-v2">
  <AnnouncementBarBadge>New</AnnouncementBarBadge>
  <AnnouncementBarMessage>The directory now lists guestbooks.</AnnouncementBarMessage>
  <AnnouncementBarLink href="/changelog">Read more</AnnouncementBarLink>
</AnnouncementBar>
notes: Give the bar an id to remember a dismissal in localStorage; change the id for the next announcement. Without an id it only hides until the page reloads. resetAnnouncementBar(id) forgets a dismissal.
Variants: default (card), primary (orange) and subtle. The bar is a labelled region and the dismiss button has an accessible name.

name: empty
title: Empty
description: An empty state with an icon in a grid-patterned square, a display title that ends in an orange period, a short description and actions.
usage:
<Empty>
  <EmptyHeader>
    <EmptyMedia>
      <Bot />
    </EmptyMedia>
    <EmptyTitle>No turtles yet</EmptyTitle>
    <EmptyDescription>Pair one to see it here.</EmptyDescription>
  </EmptyHeader>
  <EmptyContent>
    <Button>Pair a turtle</Button>
  </EmptyContent>
</Empty>
notes: EmptyTitle adds the orange period itself, so write the title without one.

name: progress
title: Progress
description: A thin orange bar on a dark 2px to 6px track, modeled on the turtle fuel gauge.
notes: Use size="sm", "default" or "lg" for a 2px, 4px or 6px track. Pass indicatorClassName to recolor the bar, for example bg-destructive when a value is low.

name: skeleton
title: Skeleton
description: A pulsing placeholder block to hold space while content loads.

name: sonner
title: Sonner
description: Toast notifications from the sonner package, dressed in Lantern colors with a hard offset shadow and lucide status icons.
notes: Mount <Toaster /> once in your root layout, then call toast() from any client component. The toaster is always dark, so it does not need next-themes.

name: spinner
title: Spinner
description: A spinning orange loader, plus a block spinner that pulses three squares like a terminal waiting on a reply.
notes: Both spinners announce themselves with role="status" and the label Loading. Inside a button that already says what is happening, pass aria-hidden and clear the role.

name: attachment
title: Attachment
description: Small file chips with an icon, name and size, plus idle, uploading, error and done states.
notes: AttachmentGroup scrolls sideways with snapping when the chips do not fit.
Add AttachmentTrigger to make the whole chip clickable, for example to open a preview. It sits under AttachmentActions, so remove buttons still work.

name: bubble
title: Bubble
description: Chat bubbles in the Lantern style: sent messages in a raised panel with an orange edge, replies in the card panel.
usage:
<Bubble variant="muted">
  <BubbleContent>Anyone near spawn?</BubbleContent>
</Bubble>
<Bubble align="end">
  <BubbleContent>On my way.</BubbleContent>
</Bubble>
notes: The default variant is for your own messages and puts the orange edge on the side the bubble is aligned to. Use muted for other people and the assistant.
BubbleContent takes asChild, so a bubble can be a button or link with hover and focus states.

name: marker
title: Marker
description: Mono uppercase dividers and status notes for a thread, like day breaks, joins and system events.

name: message
title: Message
description: Layout for one chat message: avatar, header, content and footer, aligned to the start or end of the thread.
usage:
<Message align="end">
  <MessageContent>
    <Bubble>
      <BubbleContent>Park it at the charging dock.</BubbleContent>
    </Bubble>
    <MessageFooter>09:42</MessageFooter>
  </MessageContent>
</Message>
notes: Message only handles layout. Put Bubble, Attachment or any other content inside MessageContent; with align="end" its children line up on the right.

name: message-scroller
title: Message Scroller
description: A chat scroll area that starts at the newest message, follows new messages and shows a jump to latest button when you scroll up.
notes: Give the scroller a bounded height, for example a flex-1 child of a fixed height column.
With autoScroll it keeps following new messages while you are at the bottom and stops once you scroll up. Call scrollToEnd from useMessageScroller to jump down after sending.

name: dashboard
title: Dashboard
description: A TurtleDeck-style app shell: a collapsible sidebar with nav groups and a user menu, a header with breadcrumb and search, a stats row, a mining chart, a live console and a data table of turtles.
notes: The block owns the whole viewport, so the sidebar keeps its default fixed positioning. Below 768px it opens as a sheet from the header trigger.
The console answers help, fuel, pos, inv, home and clear.

name: docs-layout
title: Docs Layout
description: A documentation page shell: header with search, grouped sidebar nav, a Prose article and an On this page list. On phones the nav moves into a sheet.

name: faq
title: FAQ
description: An FAQ section: a heading, intro and contact card on the left and a numbered accordion on the right. It stacks into one column on phones.

name: feature-grid
title: Feature Grid
description: A features section with a heading, intro and six cards, one of them a wide highlighted card with a small terminal.

name: footer
title: Footer
description: A site footer with the brand, three link columns, a newsletter field and a status line. Columns fold into two on phones.

name: hero
title: Hero
description: The Lantern landing hero: announcement bar, navbar, a big two-line heading with calls to action, and a tilted terminal typing a session inside orbit rings. A stat strip sits below.

name: login
title: Login
description: A split-screen sign in page: the form on the left with a show/hide password, remember me and GitHub sign in, and a tilted terminal on a grid on the right. The right panel hides on phones.

name: not-found
title: Not Found
description: A 404 page with a big Space Grotesk 404, a tilted terminal that fails to resolve hub://page-not-found/, and buttons back home and to search.
notes: In the Next.js app router, render it from app/not-found.tsx.

name: pricing
title: Pricing
description: Three plan cards with a monthly and yearly toggle, the middle plan raised with an orange border and hard shadow, and an FAQ accordion underneath.

name: settings
title: Settings
description: A settings page with a section nav that turns into a select on phones: profile, hub site address and visibility, notification switches and a danger zone with a confirm dialog. Saving shows a toast.
notes: Toasts need the Toaster from the sonner component mounted once in your root layout.

name: signup
title: Signup
description: A create-account page with name, email and a password strength meter, a terms checkbox and inline validation errors, beside a short list of what the account includes.
